question: Why don't we just nuke a hurricane?

frame0.description: Scientist on the beach holding a lit bomb; a huge hurricane asleep over the sea. One continuous 2.5D shot, no cuts.

loop.last_line: You'd probably keep the storm and add radiation.
loop.description: Green clears; he pulls out another bomb and the storm falls asleep again, matching frame 0

assets.description: Scientist holding a round black bomb with a radiation symbol, confident grin
Scientist leaning back, bomb held high to throw
Scientist right after throwing, arms forward, hands empty
Scientist scared, hands on cheeks, mouth open
The bomb alone, same design as in g_bomb_hold
Cartoon hurricane seen from above, four spiral arms; face drawn in code
Row of four pastel beach houses with palm trees

beats.line: Why don't we just nuke a hurricane?
beats.visual: Scientist on the beach holding a lit bomb under the sleeping hurricane. Fuse sparks grow; on "hurricane" the storm's eyes pop open and stare at him.
beats.gag: The storm wakes up exactly on its own name

beats.line: Because the hurricane is way stronger than the bomb.
beats.visual: Squash-swap to the wind-up on "Because"; on "stronger" he throws and the bomb flies (3D projectile, spin, perspective) into the storm. Boom in the pause: flash, explosion crown, shake; the storm squeezes its eyes shut, then turns smug.
beats.camera: Follows the bomb into the storm
beats.gag: The explosion only makes the hurricane look smug

beats.line: A big one gives off as much heat as a ten-megaton nuclear bomb every twenty minutes.
beats.visual: Orange heat glow around the hurricane; a big bomb icon pops in front of it on "ten-megaton"; a clock sweeps 20 minutes, then four quick sweeps with a boom in the storm and a bomb added to a tally each time.
beats.gag: The tally of bombs keeps growing while the storm doesn't care

beats.line: So one more bomb might not even slow it down.
beats.visual: Camera pulls back; a tiny extra bomb joins the tally. Scientist squash-swaps to scared, trembling; the hurricane yawns on "slow it down".

beats.line: And the trade winds would carry the radioactive fallout straight to land.
beats.visual: White wind arrows sweep toward the land; a green fallout cloud leaves the storm and settles behind him over the beach houses.

beats.line: You'd probably keep the storm and add radiation.
beats.visual: Scene tinted green; he glows green and sweats; the hurricane laughs. Then the green clears, he pulls out another bomb and the storm falls asleep again (loop to frame 0).
beats.gag: He reaches for another bomb anyway
